summary: CPU research+analysis: rank the 3 spill-workarounds (recompute-state-from-spine, node-tiling, shared-memory h_cache) for the GDN tree-verify scan kernel by LOSSLESS risk and SPEED risk, against our current impl. Premise (user): matching native FULL launch geometry BV=32 AND num_warps=4 is the lossless target (it makes the reduction tree bit-exact to native); the spill is purely the h_cache register footprint (N_PAD=16 nodes x BV x DIM_K, worst at warps=4 = fewer threads = more regs/thread). The workaround must fit that storage at BV=32/warps=4 WITHOUT disturbing the BV=32/warps=4 reduction. Rank by which preserves the reduction (lossless) + minimizes GB10 B=1 speed cost. NO GPU, NO implementation - a ranked design to bring to the user.

research.recomputeMechanics:
RECOMPUTE-STATE-FROM-SPINE (workaround 1) — mechanics in our Triton kernel and prior art.

WHAT IT IS in our code: today the scan caches every node's post-token state in `h_cache=tl.zeros((N_PAD,BLOCK_V,DIM_K))` (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:458). A child reads its parent's cached state via the ancestry select at :461-467 (`tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache, 0.0), axis=0)`), so it starts from a register checkpoint without re-walking. Recompute DROPS that cache: for node i, instead of reading h_cache[parent], you re-run the rank-1 `_gdn_node_step` (:337-383) for every ancestor on i's path-to-root starting from b_h0 (:449-453), using the SAME `tl.static_range` + `tl.where(strict_mask...)` ancestry machinery already present at :459-467. Live working state collapses from `[N_PAD,BV,DIM_K]` to one `[BV,DIM_K]` tile.

EXISTENCE PROOF in our own tree: `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` (:546-706) ALREADY runs with NO h_cache — `# No h_cache: one (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) register tile per program, so the replay is spill-free at any tree size` (:588). It re-executes the accepted chain from the activation ring on the identical `_gdn_node_step` body (:674-688). The replay proves the O(1)-state, replay-from-activations pattern compiles and is byte-exact by re-execution in OUR codebase. The open question is the VERIFY kernel, which must emit out_i for ALL N_PAD nodes (:528-532), not just one accepted chain — so a naive recompute re-walks each node's full path => O(sum of depths) rank-1 steps vs O(N) today (worst case N=14 caterpillar depth~6, 48 heads ~165 MFLOP per the cost estimate in FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §2).

HOW TO WRITE IT: the outer `for i in tl.static_range(0,N_PAD)` (:459) stays; replace the parent-checkpoint read (:461-467) with an inner ancestor loop that, for each ancestor a in i's path, loads that ancestor's q/k/v/g/β from HBM and applies `_gdn_node_step` into a fresh `state_i` seeded at b_h0. Because tree topology and N_PAD are constexpr, all loops fully unroll (no data-dependent trip counts — Triton-idiomatic). To avoid the quadratic blowup you keep the per-node ACTIVATIONS resident (q/k/v/g/β ~1.5KB/head, ~42x smaller than the state cache per FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §2) and only the STATE is recomputed, not re-loaded.

PRIOR ART: This is exactly STree's "activation replay" (arXiv 2505.14969): "During the verification process, we only generate the output y for the input sequence, but not the state after the input... We use the activation replay method to recompute the correct state before the first rejected tokens" — i.e. STree does NOT keep per-node states; it recomputes on demand. STree explicitly keeps state out of the register/HBM path: "The kernel is hardware-aware as it avoids instantiating any intermediate results as well as the SSM states off from the fast GPU shared memory." FLA's fused_recurrent gated-delta kernel keeps only ONE [BV,BK] state tile and streams the sequence (`b_h=tl.zeros([BV,BK]); for _ in tl.range(0,T): b_h*=exp(b_g); b_h+=outer; store`) — never an all-timesteps cache. So production linear-attention kernels universally hold O(1) state and recompute/stream, confirming recompute is the field-standard answer to exactly this register-pressure problem.
research.tilingMechanics:
NODE-TILING (workaround 2) — process N_PAD nodes in sub-tiles so the live h_cache stays small.

WHAT IT IS: instead of materializing the full `h_cache=[N_PAD,BV,DIM_K]` (16 node rows) at once, you process the nodes in groups of, say, 4 (`h_cache=[TILE_N,BV,DIM_K]`, TILE_N=4 => 4x smaller, 16·32·128/4 register footprint => fits BV=32/warps=4). The outer scan becomes a tile loop; within a tile you cache only that tile's node states, and at tile boundaries you must HAND OFF the recurrent state of any node whose CHILD lives in a later tile.

THE HARD PART — boundary handoff: our tree is not a single chain. A node in tile 0 can be the parent of nodes in tiles 1, 2 and 3 (e.g. make_tree(14) parent=(-1,0,1,2,3,4,4,3,2,2,1,1,0,0): node 0 parents nodes 1,12,13 which span the whole index range; node 1 parents 2,10,11). So a fixed-stride "carry the last row" handoff is WRONG — you must carry the state of EVERY node that has a descendant in a future tile, which for a wide shallow tree is most of the early tile. That is exactly the all-nodes-resident problem you were trying to escape, just re-expressed. To make tiling actually bound the live set you'd need to either (a) re-order nodes so each tile is a contiguous subtree (a topology-dependent permutation, fragile, and the strict_mask at :462 indexes raw node ids so the mask would need re-permuting too), or (b) spill cross-tile parent states to HBM and reload — which reintroduces exactly the state-traffic HBM tax FR13 fled (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §"REJECTED": chunked/streaming state "reintroduces the +35.8% HBM state-traffic tax... same 273 GB/s pool").

HOW TO WRITE IT: an outer `for tstart in tl.static_range(0,N_PAD,TILE_N)` wrapping the existing inner node loop, with `h_cache=[TILE_N,...]`. The ancestry read at :461-467 would need to resolve to either the in-tile h_cache OR a boundary-carry buffer (register or HBM) depending on whether the parent is in the current tile — a data-on-constexpr-topology branch that unrolls but adds a second select per edge.

PRIOR ART: chunked delta-rule (FLA chunk.py / chunk_h.py) DOES tile over time and carries one `b_h=[BK,BV]` register tile across chunks (`for i_t in range(NT): ... b_h += tl.dot(b_k,b_v)`), periodically storing b_h to HBM at split boundaries (`if i_t % NTS == 0: tl.store(p_h, b_h)`). BUT that is a LINEAR chain (chunks of one sequence) — exactly one predecessor per chunk, so the handoff is a single tile. There is NO production tree kernel that tiles over tree NODES with a multi-parent boundary handoff; SpecInfer/Medusa/EAGLE/DEFT/STree all pack ALL N nodes + an N×N topology mask in ONE fused pass (per FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §REJECTED "no production tree-decode kernel does in-kernel DFS traversal; all pack N nodes + an N×N topology mask in one fused pass"). Node-tiling a tree is novel and the boundary handoff is the reason nobody does it.
research.smemMechanics:
SHARED-MEMORY h_cache (workaround 3) — hold the (N_PAD,BV,DIM_K) state tile in on-chip SMEM, not registers.

CRITICAL HARDWARE CORRECTION (rank-affecting): the task prompt and FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:58 both say "~228 KB/SM Blackwell GB10". That is the DATACENTER Blackwell number (compute capability 10.0, B200). GB10 / DGX Spark is sm_121 = compute capability 12.x, which per the NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide has 128 KB shared memory per SM and a 99 KB max opt-in shared memory per thread block (not 228/227 KB). The older FR13 docs (FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:9, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:7) use the CORRECT 99 KB cap. So the real SMEM ceiling is 99 KB/block, not 228 KB.

THE FOOTPRINT vs THE 99 KB CAP: h_cache = N_PAD·BV·DIM_K·4 bytes. At native BV=32/N_PAD=16: 16·32·128·4 = 262144 B = 256 KB per program — 2.6x OVER the 99 KB opt-in cap. It does NOT fit in SMEM at BV=32 either. Even at our shipped BV=16: 16·16·128·4 = 128 KB > 99 KB (FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:9 "128KB also > 99KB shared cap — can't park in SRAM"). SMEM-h_cache only fits once BV is small (BV=8 => 64 KB fits; BV=12 => 96 KB borderline). So SMEM does NOT rescue the native BV=32 geometry — it requires shrinking BV, which then re-enters the reduction-tree question and additionally collapses occupancy (one 99 KB block monopolizes most of the 128 KB/SM).

CAN TRITON PLACE A VALUE TILE IN SMEM? In standard `triton.language`: NO user-facing control. By default the operands of an op must be in registers; loads go global->registers. The compiler only emits `ttg.local_alloc`/`ttg.local_load` (shared memory) AUTOMATICALLY for layout conversions (tl.dot operands, cross-warp reductions) — Triton issue #6446 shows this is compiler-driven and "not user-controllable in a straightforward manner; no documented API exists for directing tensor placement." Our h_cache is touched by elementwise ops + `tl.sum(axis=1)` reductions and `tl.where` selects — NOT a tl.dot operand — so Triton will keep it in registers (where it spills) and will NOT spontaneously place it in SMEM. To force SMEM you must drop to the lower-level GLUON dialect (`gl.allocate_shared_memory(dtype, shape, layout)` + explicit `local_load`/`local_store`, per Triton's Gluon tutorials) or rewrite in CUDA C++. That is a kernel REWRITE in a different programming model, not a launch-constexpr tweak — high blast radius, and the shared `@triton.jit` body (`_gdn_node_step` :337-383) that both scan and replay inline for codegen-identity (per the byte-A/B obligation, FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md) would have to be re-expressed.

LATENCY / BANK CONFLICTS: SMEM is ~20-30 cycle latency vs ~1 cycle for registers, and the [BV,DIM_K] fp32 inner reductions would hit SMEM bank conflicts unless padded/swizzled (cf. Gluon issue #8149 SwizzledSharedLayout bank-conflict pitfalls). On a B=1 memory-bandwidth-bound decode (the 27 GB fp8 weight stream dominates ~99 ms/forward per FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES.md), SMEM read/store latency is plausibly hidden — but the OCCUPANCY hit (a near-99 KB block) is the bigger risk, and SMEM still cannot hold BV=32's 256 KB. NVIDIA's CUDA 13.0 `enable_smem_spilling` PTX pragma (shared-memory register spilling) is the closest "automatic" path but it is CUDA/ptxas-level, not reachable from triton.language, and still bounded by the same 128 KB SM SMEM budget.
research.reductionImplicationPerApproach:
The lossless bar is RAW max_abs==0.0 vs native at BV=32/warps=4. Losslessness is set by the `tl.sum(axis=1)` reduction tree (:379, :382, inside _gdn_node_step) AND the FMA scheduling — which are fixed by BV (the V-tile extent) AND num_warps (the warp/lane map), per FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN_BIND.md. The spill is about WHERE h_cache lives. The key distinction the ranking hinges on:

(3) SHARED-MEMORY h_cache — LOSSLESS-PRESERVING BY CONSTRUCTION *if* it could hold the tile. It only relocates STORAGE: the reduction `tl.sum(state_i*b_k[None,:],axis=1)` (:379) and `tl.sum(state_i*b_q[None,:],axis=1)` (:382) still run over the SAME [BV,DIM_K] operand shape with the SAME BV and SAME num_warps => identical reduction tree + FMA order => identical bits. Moving the operand from a register file to SMEM does not change the math tree. THIS IS THE ONLY APPROACH THAT IS LOSSLESS-NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION. BUT (fatal): it can't hold the 256 KB tile at BV=32 within GB10's 99 KB cap, so to use it you must shrink BV, and shrinking BV DOES change the reduction tree (defeating the whole native-match goal). So SMEM is lossless-safe but does not deliver the BV=32 geometry — it's a non-starter for THIS objective.

(1) RECOMPUTE-FROM-SPINE — LOSSLESS-PRESERVING, with one caveat. The recurrent state-handoff math (`_gdn_node_step` :337-383) and the inner reductions (:379,:382) are UNCHANGED; only the SOURCE of the parent state changes (replay from b_h0 instead of reading h_cache). Crucially, you keep BV=32/warps=4 (the cache shrinks to one [BV,DIM_K] tile, ~16x smaller => fits => the native geometry now compiles), so the reduction tree that determines losslessness is preserved. FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §2 asserts "bit-exact by construction — identical native rank-1 op order, only the SOURCE of h_j changes". CAVEAT (codegen, not algebra): the parent-handoff via tl.sum/tl.where at :461-467 flips -0.0->+0.0 exactly once per edge (the replay kernel explicitly reproduces this with `state = state + 0.0` at :645). A recompute path that re-derives the parent state by re-running the step (rather than reading a checkpoint) must reproduce that SAME -0.0/+0.0 normalization and the SAME FMA contraction per the codegen-identity byte-A/B obligation (FR13_BUG_CLASS_PLAYBOOK.md row 10: "Shared-source ≠ shared-SASS"). The replay kernel's PASSED byte-A/B (126/126, 0 spill, cubin hashes pinned — FR13_GDN_KERNEL_LINEAGE.md) is strong evidence the recompute body re-executes bit-exactly, but VERIFY-side recompute is a fresh compilation that must re-pass the A/B. Lossless RISK = low (op order preserved) but NOT zero (codegen identity is gated, not guaranteed).

(2) NODE-TILING — HIGHEST LOSSLESS RISK. Within a tile the reduction is unchanged, BUT the cross-tile boundary handoff RESTRUCTURES the state flow. If the handoff routes parent state through HBM (the only way to bound the live set for a multi-parent tree), the reloaded fp32 bits are exact, but the parent-handoff normalization (the -0.0 flip + the `state+0.0` edge behavior at :645/:461-467) must be reproduced at every tile boundary AND a node-reorder permutation (needed to make tiles contiguous subtrees) changes which physical lane/warp owns which node row => risk of perturbing the per-node reduction layout. Plus tiling reintroduces the HBM state-traffic tax (lossless-neutral but speed-negative). Of the three, node-tiling has the most moving parts touching the handoff => highest chance of a non-zero max_abs.

RANKING for the BV=32/warps=4-native-match objective: (1) RECOMPUTE-FROM-SPINE is the preferred route — it is the ONLY one that BOTH (a) shrinks h_cache enough to let the native BV=32/warps=4 geometry actually compile, AND (b) preserves the reduction tree/handoff math (lossless-by-construction modulo a re-gated byte-A/B). (3) SMEM is lossless-safe in principle but CANNOT hold the 256 KB tile at BV=32 under GB10's 99 KB cap and is not user-expressible in triton.language (needs Gluon/CUDA) => disqualified for this objective. (2) NODE-TILING is worst: the multi-parent tree boundary handoff is novel, lossless-risky, and re-incurs the HBM tax FR13 fled. Speed on B=1 bandwidth-bound decode: recompute's extra rank-1 FLOPs (~0.005-0.03% of one forward per FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §2) are hidden by the 27 GB weight-stream bound and dwarfed by avoiding one full-state spill round-trip — so recompute is also the cheapest in practice.
research.priorArt:
PRIOR ART — how production linear-attention/SSM kernels handle state-tile register pressure:

1. FLA fused_recurrent (gated_delta_rule) — holds ONLY one O(1) state tile `b_h=tl.zeros([BV,BK])` (or [BK,BV]) and STREAMS the sequence one timestep at a time (`for _ in tl.range(0,T): b_h*=exp(b_g); b_h+=outer; store`). Never caches all timesteps. Caps the V-tile aggressively: `BV=min(8,next_power_of_2(V))` — i.e. it TILES V to keep the register tile small (this is the same V-tiling our launch does via `cdiv(dim_v,BV)`, fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:812/:1500). This is the direct field precedent that the answer to recurrent-state register pressure is "keep O(1) state + tile V", NOT "cache everything".

2. FLA chunked delta-rule (chunk.py / chunk_h.py) — carries ONE `b_h=tl.zeros([BK,BV])` register tile across chunks of a LINEAR sequence (`for i_t in range(NT): ... b_h += tl.dot(b_k,b_v)`), storing b_h to HBM only at split boundaries (`if i_t%NTS==0: tl.store(p_h,b_h)`). Tiles over TIME (single predecessor per chunk) — this is the precedent for node-tiling, but it is a chain, not a tree, so the boundary handoff is trivially one tile (no multi-parent problem).

3. STree (arXiv 2505.14969, "Speculative Tree Decoding for Hybrid State-Space Models") — the closest prior art to our exact problem. It does NOT cache per-node states; it uses the accumulated state-transition-matrix structure (A_tree) to compute tree outputs without materializing intermediate states, and uses ACTIVATION REPLAY to recompute the correct state only before the first rejected token: "we only generate the output y for the input sequence, but not the state after the input... We use the activation replay method to recompute the correct state." Hardware-aware claim: "avoids instantiating any intermediate results as well as the SSM states off from the fast GPU shared memory." This is the direct precedent for recompute-from-spine (workaround 1) and is the SAME pattern our own `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` (:546-706, "No h_cache: one (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) register tile... spill-free at any tree size", :588) already implements for the accepted chain. NB STree proves no formal losslessness theorem and was validated on RTX-3090/H100 (not GB10 fp8) per FR10_PAPER_NOGO_RESEARCH.md — so its bit-exactness on our regime must be re-gated, but its STATE-MANAGEMENT pattern is exactly recompute.

4. No production tree-decode kernel (SpecInfer / Medusa / EAGLE / DEFT / STree) does in-kernel DFS/node-tiling traversal — all pack N nodes + an N×N topology mask in one fused pass (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md §REJECTED). This is direct evidence that node-tiling a TREE (workaround 2) is unprecedented and the multi-parent boundary handoff is why.

5. Register-vs-SMEM general practice: register spilling is a memory-bound-friendly tradeoff (NVIDIA dev blog / studyraid) — "a memory-bound kernel can afford, even benefit from, moderate spilling to increase occupancy". CUDA 13.0 added `enable_smem_spilling` PTX pragma (shared-memory register spilling) to put spills in SMEM not DRAM — but it's CUDA/ptxas-level (not triton.language) and still bounded by the 128 KB/SM SMEM budget. Triton SMEM placement is compiler-automatic (only for tl.dot/layout conversions, issue #6446); explicit SMEM tiles require the GLUON dialect (`gl.allocate_shared_memory`).

research.hcacheLifecycle:
H_CACHE LIFECYCLE in _tree_gdn_kernel (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:387-543). Grid = (num_vh, cdiv(dim_v, BV)) (:1500); each PROGRAM owns one value-head and one BV-wide V-tile and runs the ENTIRE tree for that slice. h_cache is per-program, shape (N_PAD, BLOCK_V, DIM_K) fp32, DIM_K=128 (:458). N_PAD = padded_nodes = next-pow2(n), CAPPED at 16 (:74-78); cat9 -> N_PAD=16.

BUILD/INIT (:458): h_cache = tl.zeros((N_PAD, BLOCK_V, DIM_K)) -> all N_PAD node-state rows live in registers simultaneously = the tree co-residency.

WRITE (:527): after each node i's rank-1 update, h_cache = tl.where((offs_n==i)[:,None,None], state_i[None,:,:], h_cache). One row (node i's POST-token state_i, shape (BLOCK_V,DIM_K)) is committed; the select-write keeps the whole tile resident (Triton has no in-place register-row store, so the full tile is rewritten each node).

READ = the ancestry/co-residency dependency (:461-467): before updating node i, an inner tl.static_range(0,i) walks candidate ancestors j. h_j = tl.sum(tl.where((offs_n==j)[:,None,None], h_cache, 0.0), axis=0) extracts row j by masked-reduce over the N_PAD axis; ancestor = (strict_mask[i*N_PAD+j]!=0)&(j<N_ACTUAL) (:462); state_i = tl.where(ancestor, h_j, state_i) (:467). So each node STARTS from its PARENT's cached post-token checkpoint instead of reloading h0 or replaying ancestors from HBM. strict_mask (:401,:462) is the tree topology: strict[i,j]=1 iff j is a strict ancestor of i (Tree.masks :43-51). h0 seeds row-less state_i = b_h0 (:460) for the root.

EXPORT (:528-532): out_i (per-node logits) is ALWAYS stored for every node i -> the verify kernel must produce ALL N_PAD nodes' outputs. STORE_NODE_STATES (:533-543) is PURE EXPORT to HBM `state`; nothing in-kernel reads it, and under FR13_REPLAY_ROUTE it is OFF (store_node_states=False, :1490-1492 dummy pointer). The cross-node state handoff is entirely register-resident via h_cache; HBM export is decoupled.

This whole-tree register residency at N_PAD=16 is the spill blocker: at native BV=32/warps=4, per-thread h_cache regs = N_PAD*BV*DIM_K/(num_warps*32) = 16*32*128/128 = 512 >> 255-reg cap (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:28-35).
research.reductionShape:
THE REDUCTION = tl.sum(..., axis=1) inside _gdn_node_step (:337-383), over the (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) state tile, reducing the DIM_K=128 axis (axis=1). Two such reductions per node: b_v -= tl.sum(state_i * b_k[None,:], axis=1) (:379, the rank-1 correction) and out_i = tl.sum(state_i * b_q[None,:], axis=1) (:382, the readout). state_i += b_v[:,None]*b_k[None,:] (:381) is the rank-1 outer-product update. (l2norm at :375-376 also reduces, over the K-vector.) These are exactly native fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update's op body, op-for-op (FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN_BIND.md:21-25) -- the MATH is byte-identical; only the LAUNCH GEOMETRY differs.

HOW BV + num_warps SET THE TREE: BLOCK_V is the M-extent (rows) of the (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) tile; DIM_K=128 is the reduced extent. Triton maps the 2-D tile to a blocked layout (sizePerThread, threadsPerWarp, warpsPerCTA). The native [32,128] tile's live TTGIR (FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:12) compiles to sizePerThread=[1,4], threadsPerWarp=[1,32], warpsPerCTA=[4,1]: the 32 lanes/warp span the DIM_K reduce axis (4 K-elements/lane via [1,4]), and the 4 WARPS are split across the M=32 V-ROWS (8 rows/warp). So for axis=1 (DIM_K) the reduction is INTRA-warp only -- a 32-lane butterfly (no cross-warp reduce on the reduced axis) -- while num_warps splits the ROW (M) work. Ours BV=16/warps=8 distributes the same DIM_K reduce across a DIFFERENT lane/warp partition + different ptxas FMA contraction/scheduling, producing ~1 bf16-ULP/node (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:11-12). Note BV=1 collapses the degenerate [1,128] butterfly -> 1.19e-7 drift (FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:6,17), proving the M-extent shape itself perturbs the K-reduce tree.

WHAT "PRESERVE THE REDUCTION" REQUIRES (the ranking pivot): bit-exactness vs native needs the SAME sizePerThread/threadsPerWarp/warpsPerCTA on the (BV, DIM_K) tile AND the same per-instance ptxas FMA scheduling -> requires (a) BV=32 (M-extent matching native, so the layout solver picks [1,4]/[1,32]/[4,1]), AND (b) num_warps=4 (so 4 warps map to the M-rows exactly as native; warps=16 at BV=32 fits registers but reshapes to a WRONG tree, FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:33). Therefore any workaround MUST keep BV=32/warps=4 and MUST NOT alter the per-node (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) tile shape the reductions run over, nor the ORDER in which a node's update + readout execute. Workarounds that only move WHERE state bytes live (SMEM vs registers) or split WHICH nodes are live at once (tiling) leave the per-node (32,128) reduction tile and its op-order untouched -> reduction PRESERVED. A workaround that re-derives the state by a different op sequence (e.g. re-l2norm order, different accumulation start) risks changing it.
research.replayKernelApproach:
THE REPLAY KERNEL (_tree_gdn_replay_kernel :546-706; batched all-layer sibling :847-1048) is the existence proof that GDN state can be carried with NO h_cache. Grid = (num_spec_decodes, num_vh, cdiv(dim_v, BV)) (:812). It holds ONE (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) register tile `state` (:609-616) -- comment :588 "No h_cache: one (BLOCK_V, DIM_K) register tile per program, so the replay is spill-free at any tree size." It seeds state from the h0 bank row (:603-616), then walks ONLY THE ACCEPTED PATH as a LINEAR chain: for t in static_range(0, PATH_COLS+1) (:624) it loads node = accepted_paths[t-1] (:634-640) from the activation ring (k pre-l2norm, v, raw_a, raw_b at consumed precision; :646-673), runs the IDENTICAL shared _gdn_node_step body (:674-688), and publishes each post-step state to a LINEAR bank column (:699-706). It reproduces the scan's parent-handoff -0.0->+0.0 normalization with `state = state + 0.0` (:645). It needs NO out (q is zeroed, :621; out_i discarded) and NO per-node co-residency because the accepted path IS a single chain -- exactly STree's path-to-root recomputation (arXiv 2505.14969: per-node state recomputed along the root-to-node path, no per-node caching, exact vs sequential).

APPLICABLE TO VERIFY? PARTIALLY -- this is the crux of ranking workaround #1. The replay's no-h_cache trick works because it walks ONE already-chosen linear path. The VERIFY kernel must instead emit out_i (logits) for ALL N_PAD nodes (:528, store of out for every i in static_range) BEFORE any path is accepted -- it is many DIVERGENT paths, not one chain. So you cannot literally drop h_cache and keep a single tile. BUT the replay's MECHANISM transfers to recompute-from-spine (workaround #1, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:13): cache only per-node activations (q/k/v/g/beta, ~1.5KB/head, ~42x smaller than state), and for each node i replay its rank-1 path-to-root from h0 ON DEMAND, reusing the EXISTING static_range + tl.where(strict_mask) ancestry machinery already at :461-467 -- only the SOURCE of the ancestor state changes (replay vs h_cache read). This is bit-exact by construction (identical _gdn_node_step op order; STree exactness theorem) and reduces the live state to O(1) one (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) tile -> BV=32/warps=4 fits at ANY N_PAD. Cost: O(N*depth) extra rank-1 steps (worst N=14,depth~6,48 heads ~165 MFLOP ~5-33us = 0.005-0.03% of one ~99ms bandwidth-bound forward, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:13) -> HIDDEN by the GB10 LPDDR5X 273 GB/s memory-bound forward; trading ~free FLOPs to make the spill structurally impossible. CAVEAT: recompute reorders WHEN ancestors are computed but NOT the per-node (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) reduction shape or op-order, so it preserves the BV=32/warps=4 reduction tree IF each node's update sequence is left identical -- must be gated RAW max_abs==0.0 at N_PAD=1 AND 16 because the ancestry-walk restructuring is the one place op-order could shift.
research.registerBreakdown:
PER-PROGRAM REGISTER BUDGET (scan, per (v-head, V-tile) program; DIM_K=128, fp32=4B). DOMINANT term = h_cache (N_PAD, BLOCK_V, DIM_K) (:458). Total bytes = N_PAD*BV*128*4 = N_PAD*BV*512 B; per-thread regs = N_PAD*BV*128/(num_warps*32):
- ours BV=16/warps=8/N_PAD=16: 128KB/program, 128 fp32 regs/thread for h_cache alone (fits <=255).
- native BV=32/warps=4/N_PAD=16: 256KB/program, 512 regs/thread -> 2x over the 255-reg ARCHITECTURAL cap -> spill-to-local (LPDDR5X 273GB/s) or "too many resources" launch-fail. num_warps=4 is the DOMINANT spill multiplier: halving warps (8->4) DOUBLES regs/thread; native's warps=4 alone is what blows the budget (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:28-41).
- 256KB also EXCEEDS SMEM (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:7 cites ~99KB shared on the measured config; even Blackwell GB10's ~228KB/SM cap can't hold 256KB) -> a naive whole-h_cache->SMEM park does NOT fit at N_PAD=16/BV=32 either.

OTHER (small, non-dominant) live registers per node, all (BLOCK_V,DIM_K)- or (DIM_K)- or scalar-sized -> 10s of regs, dwarfed by h_cache: state_i (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) working tile (:460,:512); b_q/b_k (DIM_K) (:469-478); b_v (BLOCK_V) (:479); scalars b_b/b_g/b_raw_a/b_raw_b/b_a_log/b_dt_bias (:484-510); b_h0 (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) root seed (:449-453); the h_j temporary (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) from the ancestry reduce (:463). The REPLAY kernel keeps ONLY state + b_q/b_k/b_v + scalars = the (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) working set with NO h_cache -> ~1 state tile -> spill-free at any N_PAD (:588).

OFFLOAD REQUIREMENT to fit BV=32/warps=4: must remove ~(N_PAD-1)*BV*DIM_K fp32 = 15*32*128*4 = ~246KB of the 256KB (all rows except the one live node) from registers. recompute-from-spine (#1) achieves this exactly (O(1) live state); node-tiling (#2) reduces it to TILE*BV*DIM_K (e.g. 4 nodes -> 64KB, fits) but keeps a multi-node tile; whole-SMEM (#3) cannot fit 256KB in <=228KB SMEM and Triton offers NO user API to place a tl.zeros tile in SMEM anyway (compiler auto-manages SMEM only for tl.dot dot_op operands; CUDA 13.0 enable_smem_spilling is a CUDA-C pragma not exposed in Triton + incompatible with dynamic SMEM/warp-realloc).

rank.ranking:
RANKED (best-first) for the GDN tree-verify scan `_tree_gdn_kernel` (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:387-543), goal = fit h_cache at native BV=32/num_warps=4 WITHOUT changing the BV=32/warps=4 reduction tree (the lossless lever). Bar = RAW max_abs==0.0 vs native `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`.

| Rank | Approach | LOSSLESS risk | SPEED risk (GB10 B=1, BW-bound) | IMPL risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RECOMPUTE-state-from-spine (workaround 1) | LOW-MEDIUM. Does NOT touch the per-node (BLOCK_V=32,DIM_K=128) reduction tile or the two `tl.sum(axis=1)` reductions (:379,:382) or the `_gdn_node_step` op-order (:364-383) — those run at BV=32/warps=4 exactly as the cache route. It only changes the SOURCE of a node's starting state: replay ancestors via `_gdn_node_step` from b_h0 instead of reading the cached parent row (:461-467). The reduction tree is set by (BV,num_warps) on the SAME tile shape → preserved by construction. The ONE residual risk: each node now starts from a state produced by RE-WALKING its path, and the cache route's parent-handoff applies `tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache,0.0),axis=0)` (:463-466) which normalizes -0.0→+0.0 once per edge; recompute must reproduce that exact handoff bit-pattern (the replay kernel already does, via `state = state + 0.0` :645). So lossless IS achievable but must be GPU-gated at RAW 0.0, not assumed. | LOW-MEDIUM. Re-walks each node's path-to-root: ~2.57× the rank-1 steps for the deployed 14-node caterpillar (36 vs 14 step-executions per v-program; 22 EXTRA steps). Each step is ~3·BV·DIM_K FMAs. FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:13 estimates worst-case full re-walk ~165 MFLOP ≈ 5-33 µs = 0.005-0.03% of one ~99 ms forward. Decode is GEMV-bandwidth-bound (273 GB/s LPDDR5X, arithmetic intensity <1 FLOP/byte) → these extra scan FLOPs are HIDDEN under the weight-GEMV bound, AND avoiding the spill round-trip (256 KB state to/from 273 GB/s local DRAM) more than pays for them. Net likely speed-NEUTRAL or positive. | MEDIUM-HIGH. Reuses the existing `tl.static_range` + `tl.where(strict_mask...)` ancestry machinery (:459-467) and the shared `_gdn_node_step` body — but the verify kernel must still emit out_i for ALL N_PAD nodes (:528-532) BEFORE any acceptance, so it's many DIVERGENT path re-walks, not the single accepted chain the replay kernel walks (:624 PATH_COLS loop). Quadratic-blowup must be contained by keeping per-node activations (q/k/v/g/β) resident (~42× smaller than state, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:13) and recomputing STATE only. New code, but bounded & Triton-idiomatic (constexpr topology fully unrolls). | RECOMMENDED. Only route that fits BV=32/warps=4 at ANY tree size, lifts the N_PAD≤16 cap (:76-77), and leaves the reduction provably untouched. |
| 2 | NODE-TILING (workaround 2) | MEDIUM. Within a tile the per-node (BV,DIM_K) reduction tile and op-order are untouched → intra-tile lossless. BUT the tree is multi-parent (make_tree(14) parents=(-1,0,1,2,3,4,4,3,2,2,1,1,0,0): node 0 parents 1,12,13; node 1 parents 2,10,11), so a node in an early tile feeds children across ALL later tiles. The cross-tile boundary handoff must carry EVERY node with a future descendant; the ancestry read at :461-467 indexes RAW node ids via strict_mask, so any node re-permutation to make tiles contiguous subtrees forces re-permuting strict_mask too (:401,:462) — a new seam surface. If handoff is register-carried and bit-faithful, lossless holds; the handoff logic is where a seam most easily creeps in. | MEDIUM. Spilling cross-tile parent states to HBM and reloading reintroduces exactly the +35.8% HBM state-traffic tax FR13 explicitly fled (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:18, same 273 GB/s pool) — and on a bandwidth-bound decode that IS exposed. Register-only carry avoids the tax but then the live set ≈ all early-tile nodes for a wide-shallow tree = the all-resident problem you were escaping. | HIGH. No production tree-decode kernel tiles over tree NODES with multi-parent handoff (SpecInfer/Medusa/EAGLE/DEFT/STree all pack N nodes + N×N mask in one fused pass, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:16). Adds outer `tl.static_range(0,N_PAD,TILE_N)` + a second per-edge select (in-tile h_cache vs boundary-carry buffer). Novel and fragile. | INFERIOR to recompute: solves a worse-shaped problem (the wide-shallow tree defeats the live-set bound) and risks the HBM tax. |
| 3 | SHARED-MEMORY h_cache (workaround 3) | LOW *in principle* (pure storage relocation leaves the reduction tree untouched) — BUT NOT REALIZABLE on our stack, so risk is moot. Two hard blockers: (a) Triton gives NO primitive to force a plain `tl.zeros` accumulator/elementwise tile into SMEM — SMEM is auto-managed and reserved for `tl.dot` operand staging + cross-warp reduction scratch; `tl.zeros` accumulators stay in REGISTERS (or spill to local DRAM). h_cache is not a dot operand, so there is no expressible way to place it in SMEM without restructuring it through tl.dot tricks (which WOULD risk the reduction). (b) Even if placeable, the tile at N_PAD=16/BV=32 = 256 KB exceeds the GB10 per-thread-block SMEM cap (~99 KB addressable, 128 KB total/SM on consumer Blackwell CC12.1) by 2.6×. So it physically does not fit. | N/A (not realizable). Were it realizable, SMEM load/store latency + bank conflicts on the per-node row read/write would add latency, but likely hidden by the BW bound — irrelevant given (a)/(b). | VERY HIGH / effectively infeasible. Requires either a Triton feature that does not exist or a tl.dot-based restructuring that defeats the "reduction unchanged" premise; and the 256 KB tile breaks the 99 KB cap regardless. | NOT VIABLE on our impl + GB10. The task prompt's premise ("Can Triton place this tile in SMEM?") resolves NO, and the cited "~228 KB/SM" in FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:58 is the DATACENTER number; GB10 is 128 KB/SM, ~99 KB/block. |
rank.recommended: RECOMPUTE-state-from-spine (workaround 1). It is the only one of the three that (a) keeps the BV=32/num_warps=4 reduction tile and the `_gdn_node_step` op-order BIT-EXACT (it relocates only WHERE/WHEN state is derived, not the math — exactly the reward-hack-safe class), (b) makes the register footprint O(1) in tree size so native BV=32/warps=4 fits at the deployed N_PAD=16 AND lifts the N_PAD≤16 cap (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:76-77), and (c) is essentially speed-free on a bandwidth-bound GB10 decode — the ~2.57× extra rank-1 steps (~165 MFLOP worst case ≈ 5-33 µs vs a ~99 ms forward) hide under the weight-GEMV 273 GB/s bound and avoiding the 256 KB spill round-trip likely nets positive. It has the strongest existence proof in our OWN codebase: `_tree_gdn_replay_kernel` (:546-706, comment :588 "No h_cache: one (BLOCK_V,DIM_K) register tile per program ... spill-free at any tree size") already runs the identical `_gdn_node_step` body with no h_cache and reproduces the parent-handoff bit-pattern via `state = state + 0.0` (:645). The verify-specific extension (emit out_i for ALL N_PAD divergent nodes, :528-532, not just one accepted chain) is the genuine new work and the one thing the replay kernel does NOT prove — that, plus the cross-edge -0.0→+0.0 handoff, must be GPU-gated at RAW max_abs==0.0.
rank.why: The ranking pivots on the KEY DISTINCTION the task names: SPILL is about h_cache STORAGE; LOSSLESSNESS is about the `tl.sum(axis=1)` reduction tree set by (BV, num_warps) on the per-node (BLOCK_V=32, DIM_K=128) tile. Validated against our actual code: native [32,128] compiles to sizePerThread=[1,4]/threadsPerWarp=[1,32]/warpsPerCTA=[4,1] (32 lanes on the DIM_K reduce axis, 4 warps split across the 32 V-rows) — bit-exactness needs BV=32 AND num_warps=4 on that tile (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:33; warps=16 fits registers but reshapes the tree → wrong). (1) RECOMPUTE never alters that tile, its reductions (:379,:382), or its op-order — it changes only the SOURCE of state_i's seed (:460-467: replay ancestors vs read cached parent) → reduction PRESERVED by construction; its only seam surface is the per-edge -0.0→+0.0 handoff, already solved in our replay kernel. (2) TILING preserves the intra-tile reduction but introduces a multi-parent cross-tile handoff that, for our wide-shallow trees (node 0 parents 1,12,13), forces carrying most early-tile nodes OR an HBM round-trip — re-expressing the very problem it claims to solve and risking the +35.8% state-traffic tax (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:18). (3) SMEM is the theoretically-cleanest for losslessness (pure relocation) but is BLOCKED on facts I verified online: Triton has no primitive to force a `tl.zeros` accumulator into SMEM (it lives in registers; SMEM is auto-managed for tl.dot/reductions only), and the 256 KB h_cache breaks GB10's ~99 KB per-block SMEM cap by 2.6× (consumer Blackwell CC12.1 = 128 KB/SM, NOT the datacenter 228/256 KB the binding doc cites). So the approach with the lowest theoretical lossless-risk is the one we literally cannot build, and the approach with the best realized profile is recompute. Speed reasoning is anchored to the GB10 bandwidth bound (273 GB/s, AI<1 FLOP/byte): recompute trades free FLOPs to make the spill structurally impossible; tiling risks exposing HBM traffic; SMEM's latency is moot since it doesn't fit.
rank.hybridNote: RECOMPUTE alone is sufficient and is the recommended single route — it fixes BOTH the spill AND the N_PAD cap with the reduction provably untouched, so no hybrid is needed for correctness. SMEM-for-losslessness + recompute-for-the-cap (the task's suggested hybrid) does NOT work here because the SMEM half is independently infeasible on GB10/Triton (256 KB > 99 KB per-block cap; no Triton SMEM-placement primitive for a non-dot accumulator). A more useful hybrid is RECOMPUTE for the deep/wide trees that overflow registers, with a FAST-PATH that keeps today's full h_cache (register cache, no recompute) for SMALL trees where N_PAD·32 ≤ ~128 regs/thread fits at BV=32/warps=4 (i.e. N_PAD≤4 per FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:35) — chosen at launch by a constexpr branch on N_PAD, since N_PAD is already a constexpr (:406,:1520). That gives bit-exact native geometry with zero recompute overhead for shallow trees and the O(1)-state recompute only where the register file forces it. Note the gold-margin per-token argmax probe (fr13_gold_margin_probe.py / FR13_COMMIT_ARGMAX_GATE) must gate BOTH paths since scalar metrics are blind to small-rate argmax flips.

rank.summary: Rank: 1) RECOMPUTE-state-from-spine, 2) NODE-TILING, 3) SHARED-MEMORY h_cache (infeasible). The ranking is driven by the task's own key distinction validated against our code: spill = h_cache STORAGE (N_PAD·BV·DIM_K fp32 in registers, fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:458); losslessness = the tl.sum(axis=1) reduction tree on the per-node (BV=32,DIM_K=128) tile set by BV AND num_warps. RECOMPUTE relocates only the state SOURCE (replay ancestors via the existing :459-467 ancestry machinery + shared _gdn_node_step :364-383 instead of reading the cached parent), leaving the reduction tile/op-order untouched → lossless by construction; makes registers O(1) in tree size so native BV=32/warps=4 fits at N_PAD=16 and lifts the N_PAD≤16 cap; and is ~speed-free on bandwidth-bound GB10 (extra ~2.57× rank-1 steps ≈ 5-33 µs hidden under the ~99 ms GEMV-bound forward, avoids a 256 KB spill round-trip). Strong in-codebase existence proof: _tree_gdn_replay_kernel already runs spill-free with no h_cache (:588) on the identical body — the only un-proven piece is emitting out_i for all N_PAD DIVERGENT nodes (:528-532), which is GPU-gate-at-RAW-0.0 work. NODE-TILING is inferior: our multi-parent wide-shallow trees defeat the live-set bound and risk the +35.8% HBM state-traffic tax. SHARED-MEMORY is NOT VIABLE on our stack — verified online: Triton cannot force a tl.zeros accumulator into SMEM (auto-managed, registers only for non-dot tiles), and 256 KB > GB10's ~99 KB per-block SMEM cap (consumer Blackwell CC12.1 = 128 KB/SM, correcting the datacenter "228 KB" in FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:58). Recommended hybrid: recompute for deep/wide trees + a constexpr N_PAD fast-path that keeps today's full register h_cache for N_PAD≤4 (fits BV=32/warps=4 with zero recompute). All numbers GPU-gated at RAW max_abs==0.0 + the per-token argmax probe. Hardware sources: NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide (CC12.0: 128 KB SMEM/SM, 64K 32-bit regs/SM, 255 regs/thread, ~99 KB/block), Chips and Cheese GB10 analysis (48 SMs, 128 KB L1/Shared per SM, 273 GB/s LPDDR5X, consumer CC12.1), STree arXiv 2505.14969 (activation-replay recompute, but chunked closed-form output ≠ our sequential rank-1 basis), Triton issues #4756/#6446 (no user SMEM placement for plain accumulators).

redteam.losslessClaimChecked: PARTIALLY-VERIFIED, with one mis-stated claim. For RECOMPUTE the ranking's lossless logic is sound and confirmed against source: the two reductions that set the lossless tree are tl.sum(state_i*b_k[None,:],axis=1) (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:379) and tl.sum(state_i*b_q[None,:],axis=1) (:382), both over the [BLOCK_V,DIM_K=128] tile inside _gdn_node_step (:337-383); the reduction shape is fixed by (BV,num_warps) on that tile (native [32,128] -> sizePerThread=[1,4]/threadsPerWarp=[1,32]/warpsPerCTA=[4,1], FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:12). Recompute changes ONLY the source of state_i's seed (:460-467 replay ancestors via _gdn_node_step vs read the h_cache row), never the tile shape, the two tl.sum(axis=1) calls, or the op-order -> reduction preserved BY CONSTRUCTION, PROVIDED recompute itself runs at BV=32/warps=4 (the workaround must adopt native geometry; that is its whole purpose). RESIDUAL REFUTATION (real, not moot): removing the (N_PAD,BV,DIM_K) h_cache array also removes the tl.where(offs_n==j) N_PAD-axis ops (:464,:527); ptxas register-allocates and schedules the SURVIVING reduction in that changed IR context, so RAW==0.0 is plausible but NOT codegen-guaranteed (same caveat the bind doc already attaches, FR13_BF16_FP32_SEAM_SCAN_BIND.md:43). The SMEM-specific sub-claim 'relocation leaves the reduction bit-exact' is MOOT because SMEM placement is not realizable (see smemActuallyFits). The ranking's '-0.0->+0.0 per-edge handoff must be reproduced (state=state+0.0)' is correct and IS already implemented in the replay kernel (:645).
redteam.speedClaimChecked: OVER-STATED but conclusion stands. The ranking says recompute is 'essentially speed-free' because decode is bandwidth-bound. CHALLENGE: the GDN scan is NOT bandwidth-bound in isolation -- it is a SERIAL recurrent rank-1 dependency chain (latency-bound), and recompute LENGTHENS that critical path by re-walking each node's path-to-root (~2.57x rank-1 step-executions for the 14-node caterpillar, FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:13). So 'bandwidth hides it' is the wrong MECHANISM. The right reason the conclusion still holds: the scan is a tiny sliver of the per-forward cost (the ~99ms forward is dominated by weight GEMV over 273 GB/s LPDDR5X; the extra scan work is ~165 MFLOP ~= 5-33 us = 0.005-0.03% of the forward), AND avoiding the 256 KB spill round-trip to the same 273 GB/s pool nets positive. Net: speed-neutral-to-positive is the right verdict, but via 'scan is negligible vs the GEMV-dominated forward', NOT 'the latency-bound scan chain is hidden by bandwidth'. The added latency IS exposed on the scan's own critical path; it just does not matter at the forward scale. Must still be measured (decode-TPS metrics-OFF B=4 vs BV=16 baseline) -- never settled on CPU.
redteam.smemActuallyFits: NO -- DECISIVELY REFUTED, and the adversarial suspicion in the prompt is correct. (1) The cited '~228 KB/SM Blackwell' (FR13_BV_NATIVE_MATCH_BIND.md:58) is the DATACENTER/B200 (sm_100) number. GB10/DGX Spark is compute capability 12.1 with shared memory per SM = 100 KB (102,400 bytes), max ~99 KB addressable per thread block -- confirmed by an upstream bug report (modular/modular issue #5859) where DGX Spark wrongly used the 228 KB datacenter spec and a kernel requesting 224 KB 'exceeds the hardware limit of 99 KB'. (2) The h_cache tile at native BV=32 = N_PAD(16)*BV(32)*DIM_K(128)*4B = 262,144 bytes = 256 KB per program -- 2.6x over the 99 KB cap. (3) Even the SHIPPED BV=16 tile = 128 KB already exceeds 99 KB (FR13_CACHE_SCALING_FUTURE.md:7 states exactly this: '128 KB also > 99 KB shared cap (can't park in SRAM)'). (4) Independently, there is no Triton primitive to force a plain tl.zeros accumulator/elementwise tile into SMEM (SMEM is auto-managed, reserved for tl.dot operand staging + cross-warp reduction scratch; h_cache is not a dot operand). So the SMEM workaround is dead on BOTH counts: not expressible AND does not fit by 2.6x. The prompt's '256KB?! check the number -- it may NOT fit' is correct; the 256 KB figure is right (my first-pass '2 MB' was a per-program-vs-global confusion -- the grid is (num_vh, cdiv(dim_v,BV)) so each program owns one BV-slice, :1500).
redteam.reductionMatchAchievable: UNPROVEN -- the ranking treats it as achievable but the existence proof is weaker than claimed. Register-fit IS confirmed: recompute holds ONE [BV,DIM_K] state tile (reused along the replay chain) = 32 regs/thread at BV=32/warps=4, plus the b_h0 seed tile (32) + small K/V activation vectors ~= 64-90 regs/thread, comfortably under 255 (vs h_cache's 512 = 2x over). BUT the cited existence proof (_tree_gdn_replay_kernel ':588 No h_cache') runs at num_warps=8 (FR13_REPLAY_ROUTE_BUILD.md:27,:109,:153), NOT native num_warps=4 -- so it proves 'single-path recompute is spill-free' but does NOT prove 'recompute at the lossless BV=32/warps=4 geometry hits RAW 0.0'. Worse, that same replay kernel is byte-exact OFFLINE yet BROKEN LIVE (gate-4 class: accept/event collapses 2.02->1.58, live-only wiring seam, FR13_REPLAY_GPU_GATES_BIND.md:15-21) -- a cautionary precedent that 'offline-bit-identical != live-correct'. And recompute-VERIFY is strictly harder than replay: it must emit out_i for ALL N_PAD divergent nodes (:528-532), not the single accepted chain the replay kernel walks (:624). So reduction-match at native geometry is plausible-and-register-feasible but GENUINELY UNTESTED; it must be GPU-gated at RAW max_abs==0.0 at N_PAD=1 AND N_PAD=16 (read the raw float, NOT scripts/fr10_scan_output_replay_gate.py's atol=1e-3 exit code, FR13_BV_SPILL_VERDICT.md:21-22) before being called lossless.
redteam.trustworthyRecommendation: RECOMPUTE-state-from-spine (workaround 1) is the right recommendation and the ranking's ORDER (recompute > node-tiling > SMEM) holds -- but adopt it as the ONLY register-feasible route at native BV=32/warps=4, not as a proven-lossless one. NODE-TILING (rank 2) is correctly inferior: the deployed tree is wide-shallow/multi-parent (make_tree(14) parents have node 0 feeding 1,12,13), so tiles either carry a large cross-tile live set (the all-resident problem you were escaping) or spill cross-tile parents to HBM (reintroduces the +35.8% state-traffic tax FR13 fled, same 273 GB/s pool). SHARED-MEMORY (rank 3) is correctly dead and should be hard-struck from the menu: it neither fits (256 KB >> 99 KB GB10 cap) nor is Triton-expressible. Net: recompute is the route; treat its losslessness as a GPU obligation, not a CPU conclusion.
redteam.verifyNext: ONE GPU compile+A/B test (cannot be settled on CPU): build the recompute-verify variant of _tree_gdn_kernel at BV=32/num_warps=4, then on bit-identical captured layer-0 inputs (FR12 paired-capture harness, replay ON, N_PAD=16) confirm THREE things in a single boot -- (a) it COMPILES/LAUNCHES with ptxas -v / TRITON_KERNEL_DUMP spill-bytes == 0 (register-fit prediction is ~64-90 regs/thread, must verify ptxas agrees including activations); (b) RAW max_abs of every node's out_i == 0.0 vs the native fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update reference captured in the SAME boot, at N_PAD=1 AND N_PAD=16 (read the raw float by hand, NOT the atol=1e-3 exit code); (c) the negative control is powered. If (a)+(b) pass, S1 (the diffuse GDN-scan launch-geometry carrier) is fixed at the deployed tree size; if it spills or RAW != 0.0, recompute does not rescue native geometry and S1 may be the irreducible floor (fall back to the within-floor argmax bar, not abs-0.0).
redteam.issues: holds=false because the ranking's PASS rests on two unchecked assumptions: (1) The SMEM tier is mis-grounded: it cites '~228 KB/SM Blackwell' (datacenter B200 number) when GB10 is CC 12.1 with ~99 KB/block (confirmed via modular issue #5859: 224 KB request 'exceeds the hardware limit of 99 KB'). The h_cache tile is 256 KB at BV=32 (and 128 KB even at shipped BV=16) -- both already over 99 KB. The RANK doc rates SMEM 'LOW lossless risk in principle' and 'not realizable'; the not-realizable verdict is right but the size analysis in the prompt/menu ('256KB fits the 228KB/SM?') is wrong on the cap, so the ENTIRE SMEM option should be struck on the cap, not just on Triton-expressibility. (2) The recommended RECOMPUTE's losslessness and speed are presented closer to settled than they are: its cited existence proof (replay kernel) runs at num_warps=8 not native 4 AND is BROKEN LIVE (accept/event 2.02->1.58, gate-4), so recompute-at-native-geometry hitting RAW 0.0 is unproven; the speed argument names the wrong mechanism (scan is latency-bound on its own critical path; it is hidden because it is a negligible fraction of the GEMV-dominated forward, not because 'bandwidth hides it'). MINOR: the ranking's '2.57x extra steps ~165 MFLOP ~5-33us' and register arithmetic check out against source. The recommendation and ordering are CORRECT; the failure is calling them lossless/speed-free on CPU evidence -- both require the single GPU gate in verifyNext.
